expressions.desc: This is the apparent color of the clouds when they are not storm clouds.  The alpha channel of the parameter determines the strength of light occlusion for the material (and consequently how dense the shadows appear).

This vector controls the strength of the wind along each world axis (x, y, or z), the value for which may be positive or negative.  The alpha channel can be used to uniformly increase or decrease the strength of the wind.
This parameter controls the distance over which the layout region textures ( GlobalCloudMask, and CloudGlobalPattern ) repeat (in km).
scaled for clouds at a max height of 8km  maxVisDist = sqrt(h^2+2(6371*h))

This parameter set controls both the scale of the red channel of the Noise Texture as well as how strong an effect WindVelocity has on the this noise sample.  Noise2 controls the amount and scale of distortion for Noise1.

This parameter set controls both the scale of the blue channel of the Noise Texture as well as how strong an effect WindVelocity has on the this noise sample.  Noise3 is added to Noise1 as an additional level of detail.  Noise3 also has an additional control (the MultChannel) which is used to modulate the existing noise by any combination of NoiseTexture channels.

This parameter set controls both the scale of the green channel of the Noise Texture as well as how strong an effect WindVelocity has on the this noise sample.  Noise1 controls the primary breakup noise for the clouds.
Add Noise3
Combine Noise3 MultChannel
This parameter determines the overall amount of cloud cover where positive values increase the amount of cloud cover, and negative values decrease the amount of cloud cover.
Weight By 2d Cloud Texture
Blend Profiles + Volume Noise
This set of parameters control the visibility for each of the different cloud types individually ( r = stratocumulus, g = altostratus, and b = cirrostratus, a = nimbostratus )
This texture defines the world location for each type of cloud where each channel describes a different cloud type  ( r = stratocumulus, g = altostratus, and b = cirrostratus, a = nimbostratus ).

This texture is used to break up the shapes of the clouds for authoring their general form.  Each channel of the texture describes a different noise pattern the influence of which is determined by the Noise controls (r = Noise1, g = Noise2, and b = Noise3).  The texture has an alpha channel which is unused in the material.

This texture describes the shape of the clouds as the altitue changes.  Each channel of this texture describes the profile shape and relative altitude of a different cloud type ( r = stratocumulus, g = altostratus, and b = cirrostratus, a = nimbostratus )
Global Density
This parameter controls the overall density of the cloud material, rendering them more opaque at higher values or hazier at lower values.
Add additive mask

This texture can be used to add clouds to or remove clouds from the global pattern texture in the masked region.  Each channel of this texture applies to a different cloud type ( r = stratocumulus, g = altostratus, and b = cirrostratus ).  The alpha channel is unused.
This parameter controls the strength of the blend from normal clouds to storm clouds, which have additional controls for albedo, occlusion,  distortion, and (optional) lightning effects.
This parameter controls the strength of the blend from normal clouds to storm clouds, which have additional controls for albedo, occlusion,  distortion, and (optional) lightning effects.
This parameter controls the color and (using the alpha channel) the brightness of the lightning flashes.
This parameter controls the strength of the blend from normal clouds to storm clouds, which have additional controls for albedo, occlusion,  distortion, and (optional) lightning effects.

This is the apparent color of the clouds when they are storm clouds.  The alpha channel of the parameter determines the multiplicative factor for the shadow density (lower values result in darker shadows).
This parameter controls the strength of the blend from normal clouds to storm clouds, which have additional controls for albedo, occlusion,  distortion, and (optional) lightning effects.

This vector controls the offset and rotation (about the world z axis) of the layout region textures (the GlobalCloudMask, and the GlobalCloudPattern).
This set of parameters control the scale of the CloudGlobalPattern texture for each of the cloud types  ( r = stratocumulus, g = altostratus, and b = cirrostratus, a = nimbostratus )
This parameter controls the relative scale of the lighting texture (which is used to determine the location of lighting flashes in the material).

This set of parameters specifies how strongly the GlobalCloudMask texture affects each of the cloud types ( r = stratocumulus, g = altostratus, and b = cirrostratus ).  The alpha channel of this set determines the overall strength of the effect.
Enable the use of a third sample of the NoiseTexture3D for breaking up the cloud shapes with an additional level of detail (and/or different method of breakup).

This set of parameters controls the multiscattering approximations in the cloud material.  Intensity controls the overall stregth of the effect, occlusion determines how strongly light is attenuated, and eccentricity determines how uniform the scttering is.  Each of these parameters are valid in the [0, 1] range.

The cloud scattering uses a combination of two phase functions to determine how light bounces in the material.  Phase A and B determine the directionality of the light scattering, where negative values scatter backward toward the source and positive values scatter forward, away from the source. These values are defined in the range [-1, 1].  The phase blend determines how strong the contribution of each phase is, where 0 is entirely Phase A, and 1 is entirely Phase B.

This parameter controls the multiplicative contribution to the overall cloud noise of each of the channels, as well as the total magnitude of the multiplicative effect (via the alpha channel).   In other words the cloud noise is multiplied by a factor determined by this formula:  MultChannel.a * (Noise.r * MultChannel.r + Noise.g * MultChannel.g + Noise.b * MultChannel.b).

Each parameter in this set is subtracted the respective NoiseTexture sample (and may be positive or negative).  This determines how the noise texture dilates or erodes the Cloud Layout without increasing the overall contrast of the noise.

Each parameter in this set is multiplied against the respective result of the biased NoiseTexture sample (and may be positive or negative).  This increase or decreases the contrast of the noise and thus increases or decreases the apparent strength of the noise effect on the Cloud Layout.

This set of parameters is used to control the animation of lightning in the material.  The lighting flicker adds a secondary animation to the flashes.  Dynamic lightning animation is used to determine the frequency of lightning flashes (i.e. the higher this value the more frequently the flashes occur).  Manual Lightning is intended to be used when Dynamic Lighting is set to 0, and will let the user specify the state of the flashes independent of time (mostly useful when rendering stills or when manually updating time in a sequence).

This set of parameters controls the effect of lightning on the clouds.  Source Power controls the intensity of the core of the lighting strike.  Fill Scatter controls the distance the lightning scatters in the clouds.  Fill Scatter intensity controls the brightness of the scattered light.  Lastly the SecondMipLevel controls the sharpness of the details contributed by the second lighting texture sample (where higher values are sharper).

This set of parameters is used to control how the lighting texture is masked in the material.  The lightning mask bias determines at what positions in the CloudLayout texture alpha channel lightning can appear.  The lightning mask strength is multiplied against the biased resut to compensate for lightning masks which are either too opaque or transparent.  The low altitude texture weight determines the influence of the noise texture result on the lighting mask, where higher values increase influence of the texture.
